title: From Molecules to Mind
content_html:
From Molecules → Mind

How Chemistry Becomes Memory

Neural plasticity links molecular events to psychological experience. Ion flow and protein signaling enable neurons to fire; adjustable synapses reshape connectivity; networks stabilize into engrams; systems-level circuits coordinate encoding, storage, and reconstruction; mind emerges as a property of coordinated activity across these levels.

  1. Molecules: Ion channels, receptors, and signaling cascades govern excitability and synaptic change.
  2. Neurons: Spiking encodes timing and rate information; patterns drive release of neurotransmitters.
  3. Synapses: LTP/LTD alter efficacy and structure (spines), implementing learning rules (Hebbian and beyond).
  4. Networks: Co-activated ensembles form engrams; competition and inhibition help select and stabilize patterns.
  5. Circuits: Hippocampal–cortical loops support systems consolidation via replay and reactivation.
  6. Mind: Conscious memory is the experiential facet of these coordinated dynamics.
